recipes.name: My Mom's Raised Doughnuts
ingredients_raw: 0.5 cup warm water (100 to 110 degrees F/40 to 45 degrees C)

steps.text: Dissolve yeast and 1 teaspoon white sugar in 1/2 cup warm water in a small bowl. Let stand until it forms a creamy foam layer on top, 5 to 10 minutes.
Heat milk and vegetable shortening in a small saucepan over medium-low heat until shortening melted and tiny bubbles appear around edges. Remove from heat.
Place 1/4 cup white sugar and salt into the bowl of a stand mixer fitted with the paddle attachment; add milk mixture. Beat on low speed until sugar is just dissolved; let stand until warm.
Beat in 1 cup flour, yeast mixture, and eggs on low speed until smooth. Gradually beat in remaining 3 cups flour until forms a soft dough.
Continue beating dough on low speed until it pulls away from the sides of the bowl, 2 to 3 minutes.
Turn out dough onto a well-floured work surface; knead until smooth and elastic, 2 to 3 minutes.
Form dough into a ball; place into a large greased bowl and grease top of dough. Cover the bowl with waxed paper and let dough rise a warm place until doubled in volume, 1 to 1 1/2 hours.

Punch down dough; roll out on a floured work surface until 1/2-inch thick. Cut out doughnuts with a 3 1/2-inch round doughnut cutter with a 1-inch center cutter. Let doughnuts rise on the work surface until very light and fluffy, 40 to 60 minutes.
Heat oil in a deep fryer or large saucepan to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).
Gently pick up and carefully drop doughnuts into the hot oil in batches of 2 or 3; fry until light golden brown, flipping once, about 2 minutes. Repeat with remaining doughnuts.
Transfer doughnuts to paper towels to drain.
Combine 1 tablespoon warm water and vanilla extract in a bowl; stir in confectioners' sugar to make the glaze. Spread a thin layer of glaze over warm doughnuts.

raw_recipe.headline: My Mom's Raised Doughnuts
raw_recipe.description: These yeast-raised doughnuts are so light and fluffy, they're like a sweet and flavorful cloud. Spread with a simple vanilla glaze.

review.reviewBody: If these don't rise for you like they should, either your yeast is bad or something else you are doing wrong. Please don't blame the recipe & rate it down because of your errors! Also, if the bread dough was super sweet like some are wanting, when you put the glaze on, it would be so sweet, you couldn't eat it. Try a store bought doughnut without icing. No difference. And just because you grew up in a bakery, doesn't mean YOU can bake. I grew up with my father as a rock mason, but I can't lay rock!

These were great!! One batch makes about 24 donuts. I add 1/4 t. Ground nutmeg to the batter. Self rising flour does not work at all - very flat donuts that don’t rise. Bread flour yields a more cake like donut. AP flour made a lighter donut. I filled some with strawberry ice cream topping (glazed) and some with oatmeal cream pie filling (dipped the top in chocolate icing).Maybe put the glazed donuts on a rack so the glaze can harden all over. Double the glaze and use 2 T. Water per batch.Also these are just like angel biscuits, if baked. Omit nutmeg, add a little more salt and after they rise the first time, roll and cut them in small biscuit rounds. Let them rise again and then bake at 350 for about 10 min. depending on size. Brush with butter and serve. DELISH!!

Okay, these are terrific! I do bake a good deal, so leaving the donuts to rise again once they were cut out made sense to me, as did many other comments (make sure your yeast is fresh, etc.) The recipe is very similar to one in one of my mom's old church cookbooks, a standard yeasted donut, and if you follow the steps, you will end up with a light, moist, tasty donut. I upped the temperature on my deep fryer to 375 (as per Mark Bittman of the NYTimes) and flipped them after 1 minute. I needed twice the glaze suggested, and made cinnamon and sugar rolled donut holes with the extra. 
BTW, once you melt the shortening and heat the milk, you can complete the recipe in a breadmaker using the dough cycle. Add ingredients as you would for any dough recipe (ie.start with wet ingrdients and place the yeast on top of the flour. No need to "proof" the yeast to start) Afterwards, roll out, cut out and allow to rise again for 45 minutes or so. Thanks for a great recipe.

I made these today with the help of my 6 year old grandson. I used lard and an oil fryer because newer stoves don’t let you get the oil to 360 degrees. I also mixed the dough with a stand mixer, using a dough hook for the 3’ of “hand kneading”. That worked beautifully. I boiled water in a Dutch oven and put it on a rack in a cold oven before rolling out the dough and cutting the donuts, then put the donuts on parchment paper on cookie sheets and popped them in the oven without covering them. The moisture from the steam kept the donuts from drying out during their rise. I cut the parchment paper between the risen donuts and put two or three at a time in the fryer, ON the parchment paper. After a few seconds the donuts detached and I took the paper pieces out and fried the donuts 90 seconds before flipping them with chopsticks. I took them out of the fryer after another 90 seconds to drain on paper towels. When they had cooled to just warm, we glazed them. We ate them before the glaze had set, and they were wonderful. My daughter wants the recipe and I believe we will both be making these again.

Well, we just made these fabulous doughnuts and had to let you all know how delicious they are. I started the process last night and let them raise in the fridge overnight. I punched down, rolled out/cut them this morning and let them rise for a solid hour. My cutter was passed down to me and is probably from the 50s when everything was smaller so I had a lot of doughnuts and used a biscuit cutter from the same era to make whole ones for jelly doughnuts. We made powdered, cinnamon/sugar and the glazed toppings, and filled the whole ones with raspberry preserves. This was absolutely delicious and will definitely be made again!

I have tried several doughnut recipes, but this is my favorite! I added vanilla to the dough, because the recipe is very similar to a fry bread recipe I have and I wanted some sweetness without more sugar. After the first rise, I cut them and put them on wax paper lined baking sheets and put them in the fridge for later. I ended up refrigerating them overnight and letting them rise in the morning, and they still came out great! This will be my go-to recipe from now on.

SO good! Also, I used rapid rise yeast and it worked out great. I mention it because, as you can imagine, if you don't make the dough the night before, it is almost impossible to make raised donuts for breakfast with the need to rise twice. With the rapid rise yeast I just mixed, let stand 10 minutes on my pastry board, rolled, cut into donut shapes, let rise less than an hour, and they were ready to go. Still super light and fluffy and delicious!

Great, a little labor intensive, but delicious. Good yeast donut. Would make again. The batter itself is pretty plain but tastes good. 350 seemed to be slightly too hot, they cooked really fast, but were good no matter how done they were. A few I added cinnamon to, and were amazing. Would try this again and maybe try some with small pieces of apple for fritters. Made some with vanilla glaze (milk, vanilla, pwd sugar), some with mom's choc glaze. Some we made without holes (cookie cutters) and filled with blackberry jelly, were delicious! Made 25-30.

I made these before, following the directions, and they turned perfect! Tender, crispy, delicious! I made them again yesterday using my bread machine and bread machine instant yeast. When the dough cycle finished, I put the dough into a greased bowl, covered it with plastic wrap, and put it in the fridge overnight. The dough kept growing in the fridge and I had to transfer it to a larger bowl. By morning, it had grown again to the top of the bowl. I almost tossed the dough because I was afraid the yeast might have used up all of its "oomph" and the doughnuts wouldn't puff up when cooked. I rolled it out anyway, cut the doughnuts, let them rise for 45 minutes, then put them in the deep fryer. They came out great! Don't be afraid if you want to chill the dough overnight. Just do so after it rises in the bread machine or the bowl and before you roll it out. Great recipe, great doughnuts!

I have tried many doughnut recipes in the past and all have had some success to various degrees but they have never been as amazing as this recipe.

OMG!! These doughnuts are to die for. So soft, mouth-wateringly good and not too sweet. I glazed them with the icing and it was perfection. The best doughnuts in my life. 

I will never use another recipe to make doughnuts ever again. 

I placed the dough in the fridge over night (8-12 hours) for it's first rise and took it out in the morning. i kneeded it a bit and then cut the doughnuts out. Placed them in a warm spot for an hour to rise (they doubled in size) then fried them. Came out perfect. Love this recipe to death!! Will never buy store brought doughnuts again

This is a winner every time at our house! I usually do half of them just as written and then add some cinnamon to the other half of the dough just for variety. I also make the glaze thinner so I can dip instead of spread (that's just due to laziness on my part though) Like another reviewer mentioned, it doesn't take the full 2 min per batch to cook so keep an eye on them.
Love this recipe. Only one i use now. Thank you!

These Donuts are very close to the donuts that I grew up eating from a donut shop that was established in the 50s. I've only made them twice and they were wonderful! I'm thinking the more I make them they are going to get better and better. Thank you so much for sharing this.. you're an angel😇🥰

Everyone loved them... And were eagerly looking for seconds! The doughnuts were soft and fluffy, perfectly sweet and very easy to put together. They really did taste like they came fresh from a doughnut shop! It was my first time ever making doughnuts and I'm positively chuffed.~~~For what it's worth, here are my notes: When you activate your yeast... Use a much bigger container than you think you'll need! For this recipe, I used a 2 cup container... Which quickly overflowed... 4 cups would have worked~~~I ended up substituting lard for the vegetable shortening at a 1:1 ratio. I don't know what this affected. If anything, it may have made the doughnuts denser as I see some commenters saying their doughnut holes were practically hollow and mine were not.~~~When you rise your dough, for both rises, let it sit for the longest recommended period of time (1.5 hours and 1 hour respectively). I made three separate batches of doughnuts, letting each consecutive batch rise longer than the last. The first batch (which rose for the minimum recommended time) was nowhere near as fluffy as the second batch, which itself was nowhere as fluffy as the third (which rose for the maximum recommended time). The dough had risen to twice its original size in all cases, but letting it sit for longer seemed to help for some reason. My house temperature is at 68°F for reference.~~~In the attached pic, the third batcher is on the left and the second batcher is on the right ~~~When cutting out the inner diameter, I used a 1.5" cutout instead of 1". So not as recommended... But close enough that I think I can echo what some other commenters are saying... The serving size of 24 is a bit too generous! All else the same, I ended up with 14 doughnuts + doughnut holes. If I rerolled those doughnut holes, I may have ended up with 17 or 18 doughnuts... But not 24. ~~~The doughnuts do not need 2 mins to fry, keep an eye on them!! ~~~Aaand those are all my notes... I hope they can help someone looking to try doughnuts for the first time!~~~This is the perfect recipe to start out with in my opinion :)Thanks so much Peggianne!!
My first time making these doughnuts and they turned out wonderful! You couldn't tell they didn't come from the bakery; this recipe is a keeper! Thank You!

I made them yesterday to take to a Book Club gathering. Recipe made about 24 donuts. I kept 6 for Hubby and I. They are delicious and everyone loved them. Several friends asked for the recipe. They are light and perfectly sweetened. Coated a few with glaze, a few with powdered sugar and a few with cinnamon sugar. All were a hit. Two important tips: #1- proof your yeast before using it to be sure its still live. #2- Make sure your frying oil is hot enough before you start frying so your donuts don't soak up oil.

They turned out light and fluffy. make sure to use enough oil to fry in so that the doughnuts float in the oil and don't touch the bottom of the pan. I dusted them with powdered sugar instead of the glaze.
I've made this recipe twice. Both times they came out quite tasteless. They were not light like described. Definitely dunkers. I probably will not make them again.
Impressive! First time making from scratch doughnuts and these were amazing. Followed recipe exactly and had no issues, beautiful rise!
